interactions.label: Why is cervical cancer uniquely amenable to secondary prevention through screeni

params.question: Why is cervical cancer uniquely amenable to secondary prevention through screening, compared with most other cancers?

answers.text: Cervical cancer is always caused by HPV, which can be reliably detected through blood tests

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: HPV testing is done on cervical samples, not blood. While a known viral aetiology helps, the key advantage for screening is the long preclinical progression time, not merely having an identifiable cause.

answers.text: The progression from HPV infection to invasive cancer typically spans 10–15 years, providing a wide window for detection and treatment

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. The slow, stepwise progression from HPV infection through low-grade CIN to high-grade CIN to invasion takes 10–15 years. Detecting disease at the high-grade stage allows cure with cryotherapy or LEEP, well before invasive cancer develops.

answers.text: Cervical cancer causes obvious symptoms from its earliest stage, making clinical detection straightforward

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Pre-invasive cervical disease (CIN) is usually asymptomatic and is found only through screening tests such as Pap smear or VIA. By the time symptoms appear, the disease may already be invasive.

answers.text: Cervical cancer responds to treatment only when detected before any cellular change has occurred

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Treatment with cryotherapy or LEEP at the high-grade CIN stage is highly effective. The advantage lies in catching disease before it becomes invasive, not before any cellular change at all.

overallFeedback.feedback: The slow, stepwise progression from HPV infection through CIN to invasive cancer takes 10–15 years. This long preclinical phase is what makes screening so powerful — there is a wide window to detect and treat disease at the curable pre-invasive stage with cryotherapy or LEEP.
Exactly right. The 10–15 year natural history of HPV-driven carcinogenesis provides a wide screening window to detect and cure pre-invasive disease before it ever becomes invasive cancer.

interactions.label: A 26-year-old woman taking combined oral contraceptives has a reddish, velvety,

params.question: A 26-year-old woman taking combined oral contraceptives has a reddish, velvety, granular area around the external os on speculum examination. The cervix is smooth and non-indurated. What is the most likely diagnosis?

answers.text: Cervical intraepithelial neoplasia

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: CIN is usually not visible on naked-eye examination. It is typically detected on Pap smear or VIA screening, and requires colposcopy-directed biopsy for diagnosis.

answers.text: Nabothian cyst

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Nabothian cysts present as smooth, yellowish, translucent dome-shaped swellings caused by blocked endocervical gland ducts — not as a diffuse reddish, velvety area.

answers.text: Cervical ectropion

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Cervical ectropion is the eversion of columnar epithelium from the endocervical canal onto the ectocervix, giving a reddish, velvety, granular appearance. It is physiological with oestrogen exposure from combined oral contraceptives, pregnancy, or adolescence. The smooth, non-indurated cervix rules out malignancy.

answers.text: Invasive cervical carcinoma

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Invasive carcinoma presents as an indurated, friable mass that bleeds on contact. A smooth, non-indurated cervix effectively rules out malignancy.

overallFeedback.feedback: A reddish, velvety, granular area around the os in a young woman on combined oral contraceptives, with a smooth and non-indurated cervix, is classic cervical ectropion — eversion of columnar epithelium driven by oestrogen.
Well done. The combination of a reddish velvety appearance around the os, oestrogen exposure from OCPs, and a smooth non-indurated cervix is classic for cervical ectropion.

interactions.label: Which of the following best explains why postcoital bleeding is the hallmark ear

params.question: Which of the following best explains why postcoital bleeding is the hallmark early symptom of cervical cancer?

answers.text: The tumour disrupts the local coagulation cascade, causing spontaneous bleeding

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Cervical cancer does not primarily affect the coagulation cascade. The bleeding is mechanical — the tumour surface is fragile and bleeds when touched.

answers.text: The friable tumour surface bleeds on mechanical contact during intercourse

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. The tumour surface is friable, meaning it breaks and bleeds easily when subjected to mechanical contact. This is why postcoital bleeding is the earliest and most characteristic symptom of cervical cancer.

answers.text: Cervical cancer erodes into parametrial blood vessels, causing bleeding during movement

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Parametrial vessel involvement occurs in advanced disease and causes heavier, less contact-dependent bleeding. Early postcoital bleeding results from surface friability of the tumour itself.

answers.text: Hormonal changes produced by the tumour cause endometrial shedding after intercourse

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Cervical cancer does not typically produce hormones that cause endometrial shedding. The bleeding originates from the friable tumour surface itself, not from the endometrium.

overallFeedback.feedback: The cervical tumour surface is friable — it breaks and bleeds easily on contact. This mechanical bleeding during intercourse is the hallmark early symptom and should always prompt investigation with a Pap smear or colposcopy.
Exactly. The friable nature of the cervical tumour surface means even mild mechanical contact during intercourse causes bleeding — making postcoital bleeding the most telling early symptom.

interactions.label: A 38-year-old nulliparous woman with BMI 36 and polycystic ovary syndrome has he

params.question: A 38-year-old nulliparous woman with BMI 36 and polycystic ovary syndrome has heavy, irregular bleeding for six months. Which pathophysiological mechanism links her risk factors to a possible endometrial malignancy?

answers.text: Excess androgens from PCOS directly damage endometrial DNA, initiating carcinogenesis

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: While PCOS involves androgen excess, the carcinogenic mechanism is indirect — chronic anovulation means no progesterone is produced to oppose oestrogen, not direct androgenic DNA damage.

answers.text: Chronic anovulation leads to unopposed oestrogen stimulation of the endometrium

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. In PCOS, chronic anovulation means no corpus luteum forms, so progesterone is absent. The endometrium is exposed to continuous oestrogen stimulation, driving hyperplasia and increasing malignancy risk. Obesity amplifies this through peripheral aromatisation of androgens to oestrogens in adipose tissue.

answers.text: Insulin resistance from obesity causes endometrial ischaemia and malignant transformation

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Although insulin resistance accompanies both obesity and PCOS, it does not cause endometrial ischaemia. The carcinogenic pathway runs through unopposed oestrogen from chronic anovulation, not through ischaemic injury.

answers.text: Elevated progesterone levels from PCOS drive endometrial hyperplasia and subsequent malignancy

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: In PCOS, progesterone levels are actually low because anovulation means no corpus luteum forms. It is the absence of progesterone — leaving oestrogen unopposed — that drives endometrial hyperplasia and cancer risk.

overallFeedback.feedback: The key mechanism is chronic anovulation. Without ovulation, no corpus luteum forms, so progesterone cannot oppose oestrogen. The endometrium is subjected to continuous oestrogen stimulation, driving hyperplasia and increasing malignancy risk. Obesity amplifies this through peripheral aromatisation of androgens to oestrogens.

Well analysed. Chronic anovulation (absent progesterone opposition) combined with oestrogen excess from peripheral aromatisation in adipose tissue is the central mechanism linking PCOS and obesity to endometrial cancer.

interactions.label: Ovarian cancer earns the name 'silent killer' because it produces no symptoms un

params.question: Ovarian cancer earns the name 'silent killer' because it produces no symptoms until it has reached an advanced stage.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This is a widespread misconception. The video specifically notes that over 70% of women had symptoms for 3–6 months before diagnosis. The problem is not that ovarian cancer is truly asymptomatic, but that its symptoms — bloating, early satiety, pelvic discomfort — are non-specific and frequently misattributed to benign causes, delaying diagnosis.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Well done. The video explains that over 70% of women with ovarian cancer had symptoms — bloating, early satiety, pelvic discomfort — for 3–6 months before diagnosis. The issue is not the absence of symptoms but their non-specific nature, leading both patients and doctors to attribute them to benign conditions.

interactions.label: A 24-year-old woman undergoes suction evacuation for a complete hydatidiform mol

params.question: A 24-year-old woman undergoes suction evacuation for a complete hydatidiform mole. Six weeks later, her serial β-hCG levels are rising instead of falling. She has no symptoms. What is the most likely explanation?

answers.text: Retained products of conception requiring re-evacuation

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Retained products would typically cause vaginal bleeding, and β-hCG would plateau or fall slowly rather than rise. A rising trend on serial testing after molar evacuation points towards persistent trophoblastic disease, not simple retention.

answers.text: A new normal intrauterine pregnancy

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: While pregnancy must be excluded, a rising β-hCG six weeks after molar evacuation must be assumed to represent gestational trophoblastic neoplasia until proven otherwise, not a new conception.

answers.text: Post-molar gestational trophoblastic neoplasia

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Post-molar GTN typically appears 4–8 weeks after evacuation. A rising β-hCG on serial testing is the cardinal sign, even without symptoms. This is precisely why post-molar β-hCG surveillance is mandatory — disease can progress silently, and early detection allows highly effective chemotherapy.

answers.text: Laboratory error that should be confirmed by a single repeat test before further action

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: A single anomalous result might warrant confirmation, but the question states serial levels are rising — a consistent upward trend that cannot be dismissed as error and requires investigation for GTN.

overallFeedback.feedback: A rising β-hCG on serial testing 4–8 weeks after molar evacuation is the hallmark of post-molar gestational trophoblastic neoplasia. Mandatory surveillance catches this even without symptoms, and early detection is critical because GTN responds extremely well to chemotherapy.
Exactly right. Rising serial β-hCG after molar evacuation is the cardinal indicator of post-molar GTN, underscoring why surveillance is mandatory even when the patient is entirely asymptomatic.
